subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): import legacy auth-profiles.json into SQLite store on load

question: Should normal runtime auth-store loads be allowed to read retired secret-bearing auth-profiles.json and persist it into SQLite, or must this recovery stay in doctor/startup migration code?
rationale: This is a compatibility and credential-boundary decision: automation can verify the branch behavior, but maintainers must decide whether to change the runtime SQLite-only contract.

options.title: Keep runtime SQLite-only
options.body: Rework recovery into doctor or an explicit startup/update migration and keep the current runtime no-JSON-fallback invariant.

options.title: Approve runtime fallback
options.body: Accept runtime JSON import as a deliberate compatibility fallback and update tests, docs, and security expectations accordingly.

options.title: Pause for canonical issue
options.body: Leave this PR unmerged while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100067 owns the broader migration and fallback-warning design.

recommendation.title: Keep runtime SQLite-only
recommendation.body: Rework recovery into doctor or an explicit startup/update migration and keep the current runtime no-JSON-fallback invariant.

likelyOwner.reason: The SQLite auth-store refactor and earlier flat auth-profile doctor migration history make this the strongest available owner signal for the runtime-versus-migration boundary.
